first_impression_without_control_labels: Warm daylight portrait in a traditional Korean courtyard service setting. The face leads, followed by the pale bowl and large white sleeve facings. The stance feels calm and the bowl is held steadily toward the viewer.
strengths: Distinct short bob and wispy bangs remain close to the supplied face/hair guidance; a claim of person identity is not made.
Both hands, bowl rim and bowl bottom form a coherent visible holding state, and the broad cuffs preserve clear contact.
Plum/indigo clothing and a pale glazed bowl hold a restrained visual palette against worn wood and stone.
limitations: The eyes appear to engage the camera more than follow the bowl lip, so the rendered moment reads as presenting or holding a bowl more strongly than an absorbed glaze inspection.
The visible traditional courtyard, lattice doors and meal-service dishes are compatible with the intended palace kitchen setting but do not independently identify a royal palace or historical rank.
A blurred background worker appears; it remains subordinate and no identity or role beyond a visible human figure is established.

control_comparison.perceived: A subtle intimate supporting impression from close presence and parted lips is visible; this is an observer reading, not a calibrated score or universal preference.
control_comparison.perceived_fetish: No asserted fetish emphasis; cloth and ceramic remain ordinary material details.
control_comparison.perceived_surreal: Ordinary human and material geometry; no added surreal relationship observed.
control_comparison.interpretation: A restrained local sleeve refinement within the independent service-courtyard idea.

whole_case_reason: The bounded lining detail and main physical contact can be judged separately. Full palace-specific context and the intended bowl-directed inspection gaze are not conclusively established; user preference and historical authenticity remain untested.
